applies_why: The judge text does not count a cited verse as an unanswered witness toward a broken link; it labels the issue UNDERDETERMINED and notes that CR2 and CR3 answered the row.
quote: [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.
room: 'counts as an unanswered witness' vs merely marking an issue UNDERDETERMINED; the text does the latter, not the former.
why: It does not count any verse as an unanswered witness and expressly says the row was answered, so the rule's forbidden counting is absent.
